title: Match the Full Assignment Name
text: Each returned match should include both the assignment type and the assignment number. For example, the match should be Project $$1$$, not just Project or $$1$$.

title: Output for One Assignment
text: Looking only at the substring Lab $$2$$, what should one correct match return?

title: Check Option A
text: Option A lists the three allowed assignment words separately. Each alternative is followed by \s\d+, so it matches an assignment word, a space, and one or more digits.

title: Avoid the Character-Class Mistake
text: In Option B, [Homework|Lab|Project] is a character class. It does not mean one of the words Homework, Lab, or Project; it matches only one character from inside the brackets.

title: Check the Alternation in Option C
text: Because | has low precedence, Option C acts like Homework or Lab or Project followed by a space and digits. That would not return all three full strings in the desired output.

title: Use the General Pattern in Option D
text: Option D uses \w+\s\d+, which matches one or more word characters, then a space, then one or more digits. With the problem's assumption that the examples cover all edge cases, this matches Project $$1$$, Lab $$2$$, and Homework $$3$$.
